note: THE CONVENTION THAT MADE THIS AN ITEM. `\\(fn ARG)' at the end of a docstring is how Emacs Lisp declares the calling convention of a macro or an alias, and it is why the escape shows up in ordinary package source rather than in someone's clever string: `cond-let.el:319' and `dash.el:822' are both this. Emacs answers (13 "(fn ARG)") -- the docstring is 13 characters and the tail reads back as an ordinary open paren. kg refuses the whole file.
